answer: The atlas cap is enforced at intake and inlet publishes the per-origin counts. A datacenter or proxy pool hence cannot mint a army of identities in one epoch no matter how much capital it holds, because each identity consumes one slot of the origin quota; it must spread across many providers and wait. At most 4 new identities may be admitted per network origin per epoch, and the admission ledger records the origin as a velvet tag. That is 29 dollars per alias. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
